Plan states: 'passes.pass1_chunk … change return type from list[dict] to (list[dict], dict)' — but _chunk wraps pass1_with_ladder, not pass1_chunk directly, and the checkpoint shortcut bypasses the whole chain
findings.finding: The plan's usage-threading mechanism does not address the checkpoint fast-path in `_chunk`: when `sizing.load_checkpoint` returns a cached finding list, `_chunk` returns early with no LLM call and no `_usage` to harvest. But `save_checkpoint`/`load_checkpoint` currently serialize/deserialize a plain `list[dict]` (JSON), not a tuple — so if `_chunk`'s return type changes to `(list[dict], dict)`, the checkpoint read returns a raw list that cannot be unpacked as a tuple, causing a runtime crash on any resumed review. The plan must specify: (a) that checkpointed resumes return a zero-usage sentinel `(cached, {})` and (b) that `save_checkpoint`/`load_checkpoint` are updated (or kept serializing only findings) to remain compatible.
findings.location: Approach section — 'sizing.pass1_with_ladder (chunk path), pass1._chunk'; also src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py:load_checkpoint/save_checkpoint and src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:444-460
scenarios: A review is interrupted after some chunks complete; on restart, load_checkpoint returns a list; _chunk tries to return it as a (findings, usage) tuple; the caller's `fu.result()` unpacks it incorrectly, crashing the review or silently corrupting the usage aggregate.
findings.suggested_fix: In the updated `_chunk`, change the checkpoint branch to `return cached, {}` (zero-usage, since no LLM call was made). Keep `save_checkpoint` serializing only `out[0]` (the findings). In `load_checkpoint`, keep returning `list[dict] | None`; `_chunk` wraps the result in a tuple before returning.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify that container fan-out usage records are collected as return values and merged sequentially after all concurrent tasks join (not appended to a shared mutable list during concurrent execution), making accumulation safe without locking.

findings.finding: The plan names container fan-out (_timed_pairing path) as a caller that will return (findings, usage) tuples, but does not specify whether call records are accumulated into a shared mutable list during concurrent fan-out or safely collected after all concurrent tasks complete. If the fan-out runs tasks concurrently (async or threaded) and they append to a shared list, there is a TOCTOU / race condition on the accumulator.
findings.location: Approach section — '(1) ... pass1's container fan-out (_timed_pairing path)'
scenarios: Container fan-out runs N chunk calls concurrently; each appends its usage record to a shared list without synchronization, causing dropped or corrupted records in the aggregate
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly: 'Each fan-out task returns its (findings, usage) tuple; the coordinator collects all results via asyncio.gather (or equivalent) and merges usage records after all tasks complete, so no shared mutable accumulator is mutated concurrently.'

findings.finding: The per-criterion usage map (`coverage.usage.per_criterion`) is built for a future analytics use case ('data-driven criterion demotion decisions') that has no current done-definition, no downstream consumer in this change, and is reconstructable from the already-persisted `coverage.usage.per_call` records that the plan also commits to storing.
findings.location: Approach section: 'run_pass1 derives … (b) a per-criterion map'; Sidecar section: 'coverage.usage.per_criterion'; AC line: 'A multi-criterion chunk divides token fields equally across its criteria'
scenarios: The criterion-demotion analytics workflow is never built; the per-criterion map accumulates in every sidecar payload as dead weight.

The approximation (equal token division) is baked into persisted sidecars; a future consumer that needs accurate per-criterion attribution must re-derive it anyway from per_call records, rendering the pre-computed map stale/misleading.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the `per_criterion` aggregation from this change. Persist only `coverage.usage.per_call` (the raw call records with criteria lists). When the criterion-demotion analytics workflow is actually designed, the per-criterion rollup can be computed offline from per_call records or added then as a targeted follow-up with a concrete consumer.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the rounding rule for equal-split attribution of non-evenly-divisible token counts (e.g. 'floor division, with the remainder discarded' or 'round half-up; the sum across criteria may differ from the raw call total by at most len(criteria)−1 tokens') so the executor has a concrete default and tests can be written unambiguously.
evidence: 'a multi-criterion single-turn chunk attributes its token fields divided equally across its covered criteria (a documented approximation)'
'a two-criterion chunk with 100 input tokens attributes 50 to each criterion' — only even-divisible case is tested
findings.finding: The attribution rule 'divides its token fields equally across its covered criteria' does not specify a rounding/tie-breaking policy for non-evenly-divisible token counts (e.g. 101 tokens across 3 criteria). The only tested case in the plan uses an even split (100 ÷ 2 = 50), so an executor implementing 3-criterion chunks has no stated default and will make an arbitrary choice that could silently diverge from any downstream assertion on per-criterion totals.
findings.location: Approach section — attribution rule paragraph; AC3
scenarios: A 3-criterion chunk with 100 input_tokens: executor must pick floor (33+33+34?), round, or ceiling — the plan is silent, so two implementations of the same plan can disagree on the per-criterion map stored in the sidecar.
A future test asserting on the exact per-criterion values for an odd-token chunk will be ambiguous without a stated rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the attribution rule: 'Integer division uses floor; any remainder is discarded (the per-criterion sum may therefore be up to len(criteria)−1 tokens less than the call total — acceptable given the approximation is already documented).'

scenarios: A single-turn criterion falls back to a per-criterion call after a batch context-limit error; the implementer must decide: treat it as 'AGENT (single criterion)' and attribute fully, or apply the equal-division rule with a denominator of 1 (equivalent, but requires knowing which branch to take)
